phase1.explanation:
🦀 **Common standard traits provide useful functionality.**

**Common traits:**

| Trait | What it does |
|-------|--------------|
| `Debug` | Format with `{:?}` |
| `Display` | Format with `{}` |
| `Clone` | Explicit clone |
| `Copy` | Implicit copy |
| `PartialEq` | Equality (`==`, `!=`) |
| `Eq` | Full equality |
| `PartialOrd` | Partial ordering (`<`, `>`) |
| `Ord` | Full ordering |
| `Default` | Default value |
| `From`/`Into` | Conversion |
| `Iterator` | Iteration |

**Rust-chan says:**
"Standard library traits are powerful. Derive them when possible."

**Derivable traits:**
| Trait | Can derive? |
|-------|-------------|
| `Debug` | ✅ |
| `Clone` | ✅ |
| `Copy` | ✅ |
| `PartialEq` | ✅ |
| `Eq` | ✅ |
| `PartialOrd` | ✅ |
| `Ord` | ✅ |
| `Hash` | ✅ |
| `Default` | ✅ |
| `Display` | ❌ (manual) |

phase2.errorMessage:
error[E0369]: binary operation `==` cannot be applied to type `Player`
 --> src/main.rs:9:30
  |
9 |     println!("p1 == p2: {}", p1 == p2);  // ERROR!
  |                              ^^       ^^ `Player`
  |
  = note: an implementation of `std::cmp::PartialEq` might be missing for `Player`

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0369`.
phase2.explanation:
Player doesn't implement PartialEq, so you can't use `==`.

**The fix:**
```rust
#[derive(PartialEq)]
struct Player {
    name: String,
    health: i32,
}
```

**Rust-chan says:**
"The compiler is telling you that PartialEq is missing."
